For a week of downtown client meetings in Kansas City, you want a hotel that offers a balance of business-friendly amenities (good desk space, strong Wi-Fi, fitness center), high-end comfort, and impressive on-site options for hosting clients. 

Here are the top three upscale recommendations in Downtown KC, depending on your preferred style:

---

### 1. The Top Pick for Modern Business: **Loews Kansas City Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Sleek, modern, high-end corporate.
* **Location:** Heart of Downtown (15th & Baltimore), walkable to the financial district, Power & Light, and the Crossroads.
* **Why it’s great for business:** Opened in 2020, this is KC’s flagship modern luxury hotel. The rooms feature floor-to-ceiling windows with sweeping city views, large work desks, and ultra-comfortable beds. 
* **For entertaining clients:**
  * **The Stillwell:** Excellent on-site upscale American restaurant with a terrace overlooking downtown. Perfect for a business lunch or dinner.
  * **Horsefeather Social:** A rooftop bar with great views, ideal for post-meeting drinks.
* **Amenities:** Full indoor lap pool, extensive fitness center, and a dedicated streetcar stop right outside.

---

### 2. Best for Boutique Charm & Client Dinners: **Hotel Kansas City (Hyatt Unbound Collection)**
* **Vibe:** Historic, sophisticated, upscale boutique.
* **Location:** 13th & Baltimore (Central Downtown).
* **Why it’s great for business:** Housed in a beautifully restored 1920s Tudor Revival building (formerly a prominent men's social club), this hotel offers immense character without sacrificing modern luxury. Rooms are stylish and cozy, though slightly more compact than Loews. Hyatt loyalists can also earn/redeem points here.
* **For entertaining clients:**
  * **The Town Company:** This is the hotel’s flagship restaurant and widely considered **one of the best restaurants in Kansas City**. It features a hearth-driven menu that will heavily impress any visiting clients (be sure to reserve a table well in advance).
  * **The Market:** Great spot in the lobby for quick, high-end morning coffee and breakfast before meetings.

---

### 3. Best for Quiet Luxury & Marriott Loyalty: **Ambassador Hotel Kansas City (Autograph Collection)**
* **Vibe:** Intimate, classic, quiet luxury.
* **Location:** 11th & Grand (North Downtown).
* **Why it’s great for business:** If you prefer a quieter, smaller luxury environment over a large hotel, the Ambassador is ideal. Housed in a restored 1920s Neoclassical building, it offers personalized service, spacious rooms, excellent workspaces, and complimentary local shuttle service.
* **For entertaining clients:**
  * **The Reserve:** An upscale, intimate restaurant and lounge offering contemporary American cuisine and great cocktails, perfect for a quieter business conversation.

---

### Alternative: **Crossroads Hotel** (If your industry is Creative/Tech)
* **Location:** 21st & Central (Just south of downtown in the Arts District).
* **Vibe:** Industrial-chic, trendy, social.
* **Why consider it:** If your clients are in tech, design, or advertising, this is the coolest spot in town. It features a stunning central atrium bar, **XR** (great for casual lunches), and **Percheron**, one of the city's best rooftop bars. *Note: It has a livelier, noisier lobby scene in the evenings than Loews or the Ambassador.*

---

### Pro-Tips for Your Stay:
* **Transportation:** The **KC Streetcar** is 100% free and runs along Main Street from Union Station north to the River Market. It makes getting around downtown without an Uber very easy.
* **Airport (MCI):** Kansas City opened a brand-new, modern airport terminal recently. Downtown is a straightforward 20–25 minute Uber/cab ride away. 
* **Client Dinners:** If you want to host clients *off-property* downtown, book reservations at **Corvino Supper Club** (upscale dining with live jazz) or **Ocean Prime** (classic high-end business steakhouse/seafood near Loews).

---

### 1. The Top Pick for Modern Business: **Loews Kansas City Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Sleek, modern, high-end corporate.
* **Location:** Heart of Downtown (15th & Baltimore), walkable to the financial district, Power & Light, and the Crossroads.
* **Why it’s great for business:** Opened in 2020, this is KC’s flagship modern luxury hotel. The rooms feature floor-to-ceiling windows with sweeping city views, large work desks, and ultra-comfortable beds.

---

* **Vibe:** Historic, sophisticated, upscale boutique.
* **Location:** 13th & Baltimore (Central Downtown).
* **Why it’s great for business:** Housed in a beautifully restored 1920s Tudor Revival building (formerly a prominent men's social club), this hotel offers immense character without sacrificing modern luxury. * **For entertaining clients:**
  * **The Town Company:** This is the hotel’s flagship restaurant and widely considered **one of the best restaurants in Kansas City**. It features a hearth-driven menu that will heavily impress any visiting clients (be sure to reserve a table well in advance).

---

* **Vibe:** Industrial-chic, trendy, social.

Ambassador Hotel Kansas City.responseExcerpt:
For a full-service hotel in Downtown Kansas City that excels at hosting **small groups and executive meetings**, the top recommendation depends slightly on the vibe you want, but the **Loews Kansas City Hotel** is the undisputed top overall choice, followed closely by **Hotel Kansas City** for a boutique experience.

Here are the best options, broken down by what they do best:

---

### 1. The Best Overall: Loews Kansas City Hotel
If you want modern luxury, top-tier technology, and seamless service, Loews is the premier full-service hotel downtown.

*   **The Vibe:** Modern, upscale, polished, and grand.
*   **Full-Service Amenities:** High-end dining at *The Stillwell*, a rooftop bar (*Horsefeather Social*), an indoor lap pool, a massive fitness center, concierge, and valet.
*   **For Small Meetings:** While Loews is famous for large conventions, its **2nd and 3rd-floor breakout rooms and executive boardrooms** are state-of-the-art. 
    *   **Why it works for small groups:** Natural light in almost every meeting room, built-in high-end A/V, dedicated event managers for small groups, and superior catering compared to standard chain hotels.

### 2. Best Boutique & Executive Vibe: Hotel Kansas City (Hyatt Unbound Collection)
Located in the historic Club Building downtown, this hotel offers a sophisticated, historic-meets-modern aesthetic.

*   **The Vibe:** High-end, stylish, warm, and historic.
*   **Full-Service Amenities:** Home to *The Town Company* (one of KC's top-rated restaurants), a cellar cocktail bar, room service, and valet parking.
*   **For Small Meetings:** Because the building was originally a private social club, it was **designed specifically for small gatherings and private meetings.**
    *   **Why it works for small groups:** Stunning executive boardrooms with historic wood paneling, private dining rooms for post-meeting dinners, and cozy library spaces perfect for casual group breakouts.

### 3. Best for High-Privacy & Personal Service: Ambassador Hotel Kansas City (Autograph Collection)
A smaller, AAA Four-Diamond boutique hotel located in the heart of downtown. 

*   **The Vibe:** Intimate, quiet, refined, and private.
*   **Full-Service Amenities:** *The Reserve* restaurant and lounge, 24-hour room service, luxury town car service (within a 3-mile radius), and dedicated concierge services.
*   **For Small Meetings:** Excellent for groups of 5 to 20 people who want maximum privacy and personalized attention.
    *   **Why it works for small groups:** You won't get lost in a crowd of convention-goers. The staff-to-guest ratio means your meeting gets boutique, high-touch service, and their private meeting rooms/boardrooms are pristine and quiet.

### 4. Best Creative/Trendy Vibe: Crossroads Hotel
Located in the Crossroads Arts District (just a few blocks south of core downtown, easily accessible via the free KC Streetcar).

*   **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, trendy, artistic, and lively.
*   **Full-Service Amenities:** Outstanding Italian restaurant (*Lazia*), one of the city's best rooftop bars (*Percheron*), and a bustling lobby bar.
*   **For Small Meetings:** Ideal if your team prefers a less traditional corporate environment.
    *   **Why it works for small groups:** Unique spaces including a private dining cellar, a daylight-filled studio space, and an outdoor courtyard. Great for creative brainstorms or casual corporate retreats.

---

### Summary Recommendation:
* **Choose Loews** if you need reliable tech, stunning views, and top-tier modern facilities.
* **Choose Hotel Kansas City** if you want elite food/beverage and a unique, upscale historic boardroom setting.
* **Choose Ambassador** if your meeting is high-level/executive and requires strict privacy and individualized attention.

The absolute best match for your request is **Hotel Phillips Kansas City, Curio Collection by Hilton**. 

It is the premier historic Art Deco hotel in downtown Kansas City and is exceptionally well-suited for business travelers.

---

### **Top Choice: Hotel Phillips Kansas City**

* **The Art Deco Credentials:** Opened in 1931, this 20-story hotel is on the National Register of Historic Places. It is a masterpiece of Art Deco design, featuring elaborate bronze metalwork, gorgeous walnut paneling, gilded detail, and an iconic 11-foot bronze statue of "Dawn" (the goddess of morning) dominating the lobby. 
* **Business Travel Amenities:**
  * **Location:** Located at 12th & Baltimore in the heart of the Financial District. It is just two blocks from the **Kansas City Convention Center** and a short walk to the **Power & Light District**.
  * **Transit:** It is steps away from the **KC Streetcar** line (which is free to ride), giving you easy access to Union Station, Crown Center, and the River Market.
  * **Work Space:** Rooms feature well-lit dedicated work desks, fast Wi-Fi, and quiet, thick-walled construction typical of 1930s buildings.
  * **Loyalty Program:** As part of Hilton’s *Curio Collection*, you can earn or use Hilton Honors points.
* **Dining & Entertaining Clients:**
  * **Tavernonna Italian Kitchen:** Excellent upscale on-site restaurant, great for business breakfasts, lunches, or dinners.
  * **P.S. Speakeasy:** A hidden underground cocktail bar located in the hotel’s former mailroom/basement. It has a fantastic, quiet 1930s vibe—ideal for an impressive post-meeting drink with clients or colleagues.

---

### **Runner-Up / Alternative: Hilton President Kansas City**

If Hotel Phillips is booked, the **Hilton President** is your next best option.

* **The Vibe:** Opened in 1926, it is slightly earlier than the peak Art Deco era (featuring a mix of 1920s Neo-Renaissance and early Deco elements), but it carries the same historic, grand-hotel atmosphere. 
* **Business Perks:** It sits directly adjacent to the Power & Light District, making it slightly closer to the nightlife/entertainment strip, and offers full Hilton business amenities, including executive rooms, meeting spaces, and the famous **Drum Room** lounge (which hosted Frank Sinatra and Patsy Cline).

---

### **Summary Recommendation for Your Trip:**
Book **Hotel Phillips**. It nails the 1930s Art Deco aesthetic while providing all the modern digital and practical amenities required for a seamless business trip.

Here are the top boutique hotels near Bartle Hall and downtown Kansas City venues that offer dedicated boardroom and executive meeting spaces, ranked by proximity and vibe:

---

### 1. **Hotel Kansas City (In The Unbound Collection by Hyatt)**
* **Distance to Bartle Hall:** 2 blocks (3-minute walk)
* **Vibe:** Historic, upscale, and dramatic. Housed in the former Kansas City Club building (a 1920s Tudor Revival landmark).
* **Boardroom & Meeting Facilities:**
  * **The St. Andrews Boardroom:** A dedicated executive boardroom featuring rich wood paneling, historic details, and integrated AV.
  * Additional small breakout rooms and unique private dining spaces for dinner meetings.
* **Why it fits:** It combines deep KC history with modern luxury. It has one of the best food and beverage programs downtown (The Town Company), making post-meeting dining seamless.

### 2. **Hotel Phillips Kansas City (Curio Collection by Hilton)**
* **Distance to Bartle Hall:** 1.5 blocks (2-minute walk)
* **Vibe:** Classic 1930s Art Deco elegance with modern boutique comforts.
* **Boardroom & Meeting Facilities:**
  * Multiple private boardroom-style configurations tailored for groups of 8 to 20.
  * On-site banquet catering and high-speed tech capabilities.
* **Why it fits:** It is practically next door to Bartle Hall. It also features *Pendergast’s*, an upscale speakeasy-style lounge perfect for nightcaps after a day of meetings.

### 3. **21c Museum Hotel Kansas City**
* **Distance to Bartle Hall:** 4 blocks (approx. 5-minute walk)
* **Vibe:** Contemporary, creative, and sophisticated. It functions as both a boutique hotel and a curated contemporary art museum (housed in the historic Savoy building).
* **Boardroom & Meeting Facilities:**
  * **Main Gallery / Breakout Spaces:** Features dedicated boardroom setups surrounded by contemporary artwork.
  * High-tech AV systems built into modern, art-infused meeting rooms.
* **Why it fits:** If you want a non-traditional, inspiring environment for a board meeting, this is it. It is home to **The Savoy at 21c**, one of KC's most historic dining rooms.

### 4. **Ambassador Hotel Kansas City (Autograph Collection)**
* **Distance to Bartle Hall:** 5 blocks (short walk or 2-minute drive)
* **Vibe:** Quiet, intimate luxury inside a restored Neoclassical bank building.
* **Boardroom & Meeting Facilities:**
  * **The Executive Boardroom:** A private, high-end meeting room featuring an executive conference table, ergonomic seating, and full AV integration.
* **Why it fits:** Very corporate-friendly, highly personalized service, and slightly removed from the immediate noise of the convention center while remaining close to the Power & Light District.

### 5. **Crossroads Hotel**
* **Distance to Bartle Hall:** ~0.8 miles (3 minutes on the free KC Streetcar)
* **Vibe:** Industrial-chic, trendy, and design-forward (located in the Arts District just south of Downtown).
* **Boardroom & Meeting Facilities:**
  * **The Boardroom:** Features exposed brick, natural light, custom wood conference tables, and full AV capabilities.
  * **The Paring Room:** A smaller, intimate space ideal for small strategy sessions or executive dinners.
* **Why it fits:** Ideal if your team prefers a vibrant, creative neighborhood feel over the immediate financial district. It features a stunning rooftop bar (*Percheron*) with views of the skyline.

---

### Local Transit Tip for Your Group
All of these hotels sit along or within 2 blocks of the **KC Streetcar line**. The streetcar is **100% free to ride** and runs continuously from River Market through Downtown/Bartle Hall down to the Crossroads Arts District, making movement between the hotel, boardrooms, and evening event venues very easy for guests without needing rideshares.

Kansas City offers a rich urban experience, especially for those interested in jazz, barbecue, and downtown exploration. Here are some recommendations for hotels that will place you in the heart of the action:

1. **The Fontaine**: Located on the Country Club Plaza, this luxurious hotel provides easy access to both downtown and the historic 18th & Vine Jazz District. The Fontaine offers stylish rooms and a rooftop pool with great city views.

2. **Hotel Kansas City**: A part of The Unbound Collection by Hyatt, this hotel combines historic charm with modern amenities. It's centrally located, making it convenient for exploring downtown, the Power & Light District, and the nearby jazz clubs.

5. **The Westin Kansas City at Crown Center**: This hotel is near Union Station and offers a great base for exploring downtown. The Crown Center area also provides a variety of dining and entertainment options.

6. **Hotel Phillips Kansas City, Curio Collection by Hilton**: This historic hotel is just a few blocks from the Power & Light District. It offers a blend of vintage charm and modern luxury, with easy access to nightlife and dining.

For the full Kansas City experience, don't miss visiting the American Jazz Museum, indulging in some world-famous Kansas City barbecue at places like Joe's Kansas City Bar-B-Que or Arthur Bryant's, and exploring the dynamic neighborhoods downtown.

To truly experience Kansas City’s trio of **Jazz, Barbecue, and Downtown Discovery**, your best base is the **Crossroads Arts District** or the **Historic Downtown Core**. These areas put you directly on the **KC Streetcar line** (which is 100% free to ride) and place you minutes from legendary jazz clubs and world-class pitmasters.

Here are the top urban hotels tailored specifically to that itinerary, followed by a quick guide on how to pull the trip together.

---

### The Top Hotel Picks

#### 1. The Ultimate Urban Choice: **Crossroads Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Industrial-chic, hyper-local, and effortlessly cool.
* **The Experience:** Housed in a former Pabst Brewing bottling plant, this boutique hotel features exposed brick, local artwork, and a bustling lobby scene. Its rooftop bar offer sweeping skyline views of downtown.
* **Why it fits your trip:** 
  * **Jazz:** A 5-minute walk or streetcar ride to **Green Lady Lounge** (one of the best retro jazz clubs in America).
  * **BBQ:** Walk two blocks to **Jack Stack BBQ** (Freighthouse location) for upscale burnt ends and ribs. 
  * **Discovery:** Located in the heart of the Crossroads, surrounded by art galleries, microbreweries, and boutique shopping.

#### 2. The Historic & Speakeasy Vibe: **Hotel Phillips Kansas City (Curio Collection)**
* **Vibe:** 1930s Art Deco elegance meet modern luxury.
* **The Experience:** Step back into KC’s Prohibition era (when Tom Pendergast ruled the city and jazz flourished). It features a soaring lobby with a 11-foot statue of the Goddess of Dawn and an underground speakeasy, **Pendergast Club**.
* **Why it fits your trip:**
  * **Jazz:** Walk right downstairs to their lounge or walk two blocks to **The Majestic**, a historic steakhouse featuring live jazz in a former speakeasy basement.
  * **BBQ:** Quick streetcar ride to the Power & Light District or short Uber to historic BBQ joints.
  * **Discovery:** Central downtown location, steps from the Streetcar and the historic Financial District.

#### 3. For Art & History Lovers: **21c Museum Hotel Kansas City**
* **Vibe:** Contemporary art museum meets boutique hotel.
* **The Experience:** Located in the historic Savoy building (where Harry S. Truman frequented), this property functions as a 24/7 free contemporary art gallery. It blends modern, avant-garde interior design with restored 19th-century architecture.
* **Why it fits your trip:**
  * **Jazz & Food:** Features *The Savoy*, an iconic restaurant serving classic cocktails and high-end fare in historic booths.
  * **Discovery:** Located in the West Loop, ideal for exploring downtown architecture, the Library District (check out the "Community Bookshelf" garage), and the River Market.

---

### How to Execute Your KC Trip

#### 🎷 The Jazz Route
* **Green Lady Lounge (Crossroads):** Velvet walls, low lights, no cover charge, and live jazz 365 days a year. 
* **The Black Dolphin (Crossroads):** Right next door to Green Lady; slightly more modern, hip jazz vibe.
* **18th & Vine Historic District:** Take a 5-minute Uber from downtown to the birthplace of KC Jazz. Visit the **American Jazz Museum** by day, and hit the **Mutual Musicians Foundation** late night (open past 2 AM on weekends for raw, authentic jam sessions).

#### 🍖 The Barbecue Hit List (Near Downtown)
* **Jack Stack BBQ (Freighthouse / Crossroads):** Known for hickory-smoked ribs, lamb ribs, and legendary cheesy corn bake. Great sit-down atmosphere.
* **Char Bar (Midtown/Plaza area):** Modern smokehouse with a massive outdoor beer garden, famous for burnt end bennies and pulled pork.
* **Arthur Bryant’s (18th & Vine area):** The gritty, legendary granddaddy of KC BBQ. Gritty, historic, and famous for its tangy, vinegar-based sauce. (Presidential favorite).
* **Joe’s Kansas City Bar-B-Que (Gas Station location):** A 10-minute ride outside downtown, but mandatory for first-timers. Get the **Z-Man Sandwich** (brisket, smoked provolone, onion rings on a Kaiser roll).

#### 🏙️ Downtown Discovery Highlights
* **Ride the KC Streetcar:** It runs along Main Street from the **River Market** (great open-air weekend market) down through Downtown, the Power & Light District, Crossroads, and ends at **Union Station**.
* **Union Station & National WWI Museum:** Walk through the grand train hall at Union Station, then head up the hill to the WWI Museum tower for the single best panoramic view of the Kansas City skyline.
* **First Fridays (If timing permits):** If you are there on the first Friday of the month, the Crossroads neighborhood transforms into a massive street festival with gallery walk-throughs, food trucks, and street performers.

The single best hotel for exploring jazz, barbecue, and nightlife in Kansas City is **The Crossroads Hotel**. 

While technically in the Crossroads Arts District (immediately adjacent to Downtown proper), this location is the absolute sweet spot for what you want to experience. 

Here is the breakdown of why it is the top choice, along with a few excellent alternatives depending on your style.

---

### **#1 Overall Pick: The Crossroads Hotel**
* **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, trendy, and deeply tied to local KC culture. It features a bustling lobby bar, an artistic atmosphere, and one of the best rooftop bars in the city (Percheron).
* **Why it’s perfect for Jazz:** You are a 5-minute walk from **Green Lady Lounge** and **Black Dolphin**, two of the best, most authentic velvet-draped jazz clubs in the country (featuring live jazz 365 days a year with no cover charge). 
* **Why it’s perfect for BBQ:** You are two blocks from **Fiorella’s Jack Stack BBQ (Freight House location)**, famous for burnt ends and lamb ribs in a historic train depot setting.
* **Why it’s perfect for Nightlife:** The hotel sits in the heart of the Crossroads, home to craft breweries, speakeasies (like *Thou Mayest* and *Swordfish Tom's*), and cocktail dens. 
* **Bonus:** It is steps away from the **KC Streetcar** (which is 100% **free** to ride), taking you north into Downtown/Power & Light or south to Union Station.

---

### **Runner-Up Options (Depending on Your Style)**

#### **2. For Historic Glamour & Speakeasies: Hotel Kansas City (Unbound Collection by Hyatt)**
* **The Vibe:** Located in a beautifully restored 1920s Tudor Revival club building in the heart of Downtown. It oozes Old-World charm.
* **Nightlife & Jazz:** It houses **The Nighthawk**, a subterranean basement bar/speakeasy with live music, vinyl nights, and late-night drinks. It is also a short walk to **The Phoenix**, a historic Downtown jazz and blues joint with legendary weekend brunch.
* **Location:** Right next to the **Power & Light District** (KC’s massive high-energy entertainment and bar cluster).

#### **3. For Modern Luxury & Views: Loews Kansas City**
* **The Vibe:** Sleek, brand-new, ultra-modern tower with high-end amenities, a massive indoor pool, and great skyline views.
* **Nightlife:** Home to **The Horsefeather Lounge**, a sophisticated lounge right in the lobby.
* **Location:** Perfectly situated right on the border of Downtown and the Crossroads, giving you equal walking access to the quiet cocktail lounges of the Crossroads and the wild party atmosphere of Power & Light.

#### **4. For Classic Downtown Vibe: Hotel Phillips (Curio Collection by Hilton)**
* **The Vibe:** Art Deco gem built in the 1930s.
* **Nightlife:** It features **P.S. Speakeasy**, an underground cocktail bar hidden behind a fake door in the basement, reminiscent of Prohibition-era KC when jazz and booze flowed freely under Boss Tom Pendergast.

---

### **Quick Cheat-Sheet for Your Trip:**

* **The Free KC Streetcar:** No matter which downtown hotel you choose, use the streetcar to get around. It runs down Main Street connecting River Market, Downtown, Power & Light, and Crossroads.
* **Must-Visit Jazz Spots:**
  1. *Green Lady Lounge* (Crossroads - classic, vintage vibe)
  2. *The Phoenix* (Downtown - great blues/jazz brunch)
  3. *Mutual Musicians Foundation* (18th & Vine - late-night jams after 1 AM on weekends; take a 5-min Uber here).
* **Must-Eat BBQ near Downtown:**
  1. *Jack Stack Freight House* (Crossroads - sit-down, upscale)
  2. *County Road Ice House* (Power & Light - a partnership with legendary Joe's KC BBQ)
  3. *Arthur Bryant’s* (18th & Vine area - 5-minute Uber, pure history and heavy smoke)
* **Nightlife Hubs:**
  * **Crossroads:** Craft beer, speakeasies, jazz, chill lounge vibes.
  * **Power & Light (P&L):** Arena-style multi-venue party block, country bars, dance clubs.

Staying near the Power & Light (P&L) District puts you steps away from Kansas City’s premier entertainment hub, which features over 50 bars, restaurants, live music venues (like the KC Live! Block), and the T-Mobile Center. 

Here are the best places to stay near the Power & Light District, categorized by the vibe and experience you’re looking for:

---

### 1. Directly in the Action (1–3 Minute Walk)

**Hilton President Kansas City**
* **Vibe:** Historic elegance with a lively lounge scene.
* **Why stay here:** It is literally located on the edge of the Power & Light District (14th & Baltimore). You can walk out the front door and be at the bars in seconds. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** Home to **The Drum Room**, a historic cocktail lounge that has hosted Frank Sinatra and Patsy Cline and still features live music and great drinks.

**Hotel Phillips Kansas City (Curio Collection by Hilton)**
* **Vibe:** 1920s Art Deco glam with a sultry, hidden nightlife scene.
* **Why stay here:** Located just 2 blocks from P&L, this historic hotel offers high-end accommodations with a lot of character.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** It houses **P.S. Speakeasy**, an underground, prohibition-style cocktail lounge hidden behind a fake door in the basement—perfect for a late-night nightcap.

---

### 2. High-End & Modern Luxury (3–5 Minute Walk)

**Loews Kansas City Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Modern, upscale, and buzzing with energy.
* **Why stay here:** This is one of KC’s newest and grandest hotels. It features an indoor lap pool, floor-to-ceiling skyline views, and a massive lobby bar. It’s a 5-minute walk to P&L and connected via a skybridge to the Convention Center.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** **Horsefeather Social**, the hotel's 7th-floor outdoor terrace bar, offers incredible views of downtown and the Kauffman Center, making it a top spot for pre-game or pre-concert drinks.

---

### 3. Best Value & Convenience (On the Streetcar Line)

**Courtyard & Residence Inn Kansas City Downtown/Convention Center**
* **Vibe:** Modern, reliable, and practical.
* **Why stay here:** These two Marriott properties share a single building just 2 blocks west of P&L. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** There is a **KC Streetcar stop right outside the door**. The Streetcar is **100% free** and runs late on weekends, allowing you to easily hop between Power & Light and the trendy Crossroads Arts District just south.

---

### 4. Alternative Nightlife Scene: The Crossroads District (5 Minutes Away via Free Streetcar)

If you want a slightly more craft-cocktail, microbrewery, and indie-music vibe while still being a 2-minute streetcar ride from Power & Light, stay just south in the **Crossroads Arts District**.

**Crossroads Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Ultra-trendy, industrial-chic, and boutique.
* **Why stay here:** Located about 6 blocks south of P&L (a 10-minute walk or a 2-minute free Streetcar ride). It is surrounded by KC’s best local breweries and cocktail bars.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** Home to **Percheron**, one of the best rooftop bars in Kansas City, offering craft beer, frozen cocktails, and panoramic views of the city.

---

### Pro-Tips for Staying Near P&L for Nightlife:

1. **Use the KC Streetcar:** It’s completely free, runs along Main Street, and operates until 1:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays. It connects P&L to Union Station, River Market, and the Crossroads.
2. **Book Ahead for Major Events:** If there is a big concert or sporting event at the **T-Mobile Center** or a Chiefs/Royals victory rally, hotels right in P&L sell out months in advance and raise rates significantly.

Here are the best places to stay near the Power & Light District, categorized by the vibe and experience you’re looking for:

---

### 1. Directly in the Action (1–3 Minute Walk)

**Hilton President Kansas City**
* **Vibe:** Historic elegance with a lively lounge scene.
* **Why stay here:** It is literally located on the edge of the Power & Light District (14th & Baltimore). You can walk out the front door and be at the bars in seconds. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** Home to **The Drum Room**, a historic cocktail lounge that has hosted Frank Sinatra and Patsy Cline and still features live music and great drinks.

**Hotel Phillips Kansas City (Curio Collection by Hilton)**
* **Vibe:** 1920s Art Deco glam with a sultry, hidden nightlife scene.
* **Why stay here:** Located just 2 blocks from P&L, this historic hotel offers high-end accommodations with a lot of character.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** It houses **P.S. Speakeasy**, an underground, prohibition-style cocktail lounge hidden behind a fake door in the basement—perfect for a late-night nightcap.

---

### 2. High-End & Modern Luxury (3–5 Minute Walk)

**Loews Kansas City Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Modern, upscale, and buzzing with energy.
* **Why stay here:** This is one of KC’s newest and grandest hotels. It features an indoor lap pool, floor-to-ceiling skyline views, and a massive lobby bar. It’s a 5-minute walk to P&L and connected via a skybridge to the Convention Center.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** **Horsefeather Social**, the hotel's 7th-floor outdoor terrace bar, offers incredible views of downtown and the Kauffman Center, making it a top spot for pre-game or pre-concert drinks.

---

### 3. Best Value & Convenience (On the Streetcar Line)

**Courtyard & Residence Inn Kansas City Downtown/Convention Center**
* **Vibe:** Modern, reliable, and practical.
* **Why stay here:** These two Marriott properties share a single building just 2 blocks west of P&L. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** There is a **KC Streetcar stop right outside the door**. The Streetcar is **100% free** and runs late on weekends, allowing you to easily hop between Power & Light and the trendy Crossroads Arts District just south.

---

If you want a slightly more craft-cocktail, microbrewery, and indie-music vibe while still being a 2-minute streetcar ride from Power & Light, stay just south in the **Crossroads Arts District**.

**Crossroads Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Ultra-trendy, industrial-chic, and boutique.

---

- **Pros:** Contemporary art throughout, unique experience, great restaurant (Savoy), stylish rooms

- **Location:** Walnut Street, walkable to dining
- **Best if:** You want a conversation-starting, culturally rich stay

---

- **Cons:** Older property, rooms vary in quality
- **Location:** Central downtown
- **Best if:** You love historic hotels with personality

---

### 🌇 The Fontaine
- **Pros:** Rooftop pool & bar, modern design, great views, popular social scene
- **Cons:** Can be noisy on weekends, parking costs extra
- **Location:** Country Club Plaza area *(slightly south of core downtown)*
- **Best if:** You want a trendy, Instagram-worthy stay near shopping

---

### 🛏️ Marriott KC Downtown
- **Pros:** Large rooms, reliable quality, Skywalk access, good loyalty points
- **Cons:** Less local character, standard chain feel
- **Location:** Connected to Sprint Center area

All options are within a short rideshare to KC's famous BBQ spots (Joe's, Q39, Jack Stack)

- ✅ Many hotels offer **free cancellation** if you book early

---

*Prices are estimates and vary by season/availability. Always verify current rates on hotel websites or booking platforms.*

Kansas City’s massive convention hotels (like the Loews or the Downtown Marriott) offer scale, but they often lack a sense of place. If you are looking for accommodations that honor KC’s rich architectural heritage—from its Jazz Age boom and political boss scandals to its industrial rail history—while offering high-end, contemporary interior design, several exceptional alternatives stand out.

Here are the best design- and history-forward boutique alternatives in Kansas City, categorized by their distinct aesthetic and historic profiles.

---

### 1. The Industrial-Historic Icon: **Crossroads Hotel**
* **The History:** Located in the heart of the Crossroads Arts District, the hotel occupies two adjacent historic buildings: the 1911 Pabst Brewing Depot and the 1919 Blatz Bottling Plant. During Prohibition, political boss Tom Pendergast used the neighborhood’s underground vaults for illicit operations. 
* **The Design:** A masterclass in modern industrial preservation. Chicago-based studio El Dorado retained original heavy timber beams, exposed brick, original iron fire doors, and brick vaults, softening them with custom leather, velvet furnishings, and warm lighting. 
* **The Vibe:** Creative, energetic, and deeply local. 
* **Highlights:** 
  * A central, glass-roofed atrium (the former alleyway between the buildings).
  * An in-house art gallery featuring rotating local artists.
  * **Percheron**, one of the best rooftop cocktail bars in the city, offering panoramic views of Union Station and the downtown skyline.

### 2. The Gilded Age Meets Contemporary Art: **21c Museum Hotel (The Savoy)**
* **The History:** Housed in the historic Savoy Building (built in 1888), this is one of the oldest standing hotel structures west of the Mississippi. Its famous restaurant, **The Savoy Grill**, opened in 1903 and was a favorite haunt of President Harry S. Truman (his favorite booth is preserved).
* **The Design:** A bold juxtaposition of 19th-century Victorian and Arts & Crafts architecture with cutting-edge, 21st-century museum design. Original stained glass, ornate woodwork, and historic murals by Edward Holmdahl exist alongside contemporary art installations curated by 21c.
* **The Vibe:** Intellectual, avant-garde, and immersive.
* **Highlights:** 
  * The hotel functions as a free, 24/7 contemporary art museum with over 6,000 square feet of exhibition space.
  * The rooms feature high ceilings, original architectural details, and sleek, minimalist custom furniture.

### 3. The Art Deco Masterpiece: **Hotel Phillips**
* **The History:** Opened in 1931 at the height of Kansas City’s Art Deco building boom, the 20-story Hotel Phillips was once the tallest building in the city. It catered to the era's elite, from politicians to touring jazz musicians.
* **The Design:** A recent multi-million dollar restoration meticulously preserved its 1930s grandeur. The lobby features 11-foot gilded bronze light fixtures, black walnut paneling, original marble, and a stunning 11-foot bronze statue of "Dawn," the goddess of the morning, standing at the top of the grand staircase.
* **The Vibe:** Classic, refined Jazz Age elegance.
* **Highlights:** 
  * **Pendergast Club:** A moody, velvet-draped speakeasy hidden behind a secret door, serving classic cocktails and fine cigars.
  * Located right in the Downtown Loop, minutes from the convention center, but with a intimate, boutique feel.

### 4. The Modernist Mansion: **The Truitt**
* **The History:** Located in the Southmoreland neighborhood near the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, this 1910 Colonial Revival mansion was originally built as a grand private estate. 
* **The Design:** A modern-maximalist transformation. Designed by local studio *Selection*, the interiors ditch traditional B&B clichés for sophisticated wallpaper, custom mid-century modern lighting, rich jewel tones, and curated vintage art. 
* **The Vibe:** Residential luxury; feels like staying at the impossibly chic home of a wealthy art collector.
* **Highlights:** 
  * An intimate 8-room property that offers maximum privacy.
  * Beautiful historic sunrooms and lush garden grounds.
  * Located away from downtown, placing you within walking distance of KC's best cultural institutions.

### 5. The Micro-Boutique: **No Vacancy**
* **The History:** Set on the second floor of an 1800s brick building on Wyandotte Street in the Crossroads Arts District, this space served various commercial purposes over a century before being converted into an independent hotel.
* **The Design:** Highly curated, vintage-inspired residential design. Each of the 8 guest rooms features distinct color palettes, local artwork, retro light fixtures, and plush textiles. It bridges the gap between a high-design boutique hotel and an exclusive private guesthouse.
* **The Vibe:** Cool, artistic, and secretive. 
* **Highlights:** 
  * A central lounge and a private, plant-filled second-story courtyard for guests.
  * Entirely tech-enabled (keyless entry), giving it an intimate, "un-hotel" feel.

---

### Quick Comparison Guide

| Hotel | Neighborhood | Style Profile | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Crossroads Hotel** | Crossroads Arts | Industrial / Local Craft | Rooftop drinks, vibrant social scene, proximity to streetcar |
| **21c Kansas City** | Downtown/Garment | Avant-Garde / Victorian | Art lovers, history buffs, culinary travelers |
| **Hotel Phillips** | Downtown Loop | 1930s Art Deco | Classic luxury, close walk to convention center |
| **The Truitt** | Midtown / Plaza | Colonial Revival / Maximalist | A quiet, design-led retreat near world-class museums |
| **No Vacancy** | Crossroads Arts | Retro-Modern / Bohemian | Creatives, solo travelers, small group buyouts |

The absolute best match for your request is **Hotel Phillips Kansas City, Curio Collection by Hilton**. 

It hits every single detail you are looking for: it is deeply historic, dripping with romantic 1930s glamour, and houses one of the best hidden speakeasies in the city.

Here is the breakdown of why this is your best option, along with a top runner-up:

---

### The Top Choice: **Hotel Phillips Kansas City**

* **The Romantic & Historic Vibe:** Opened in 1931 during the height of Kansas City’s mob-ruled "Pendergast Era," Hotel Phillips is an Art Deco masterpiece listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The lobby features dark wood paneling, rich velvet, glowing vintage light fixtures, and an iconic 11-foot bronze statue of Dawn, the Goddess of a New Day. It feels moody, intimate, and sophisticated.
* **The Speakeasy:** **P.S. Speakeasy (PS Lounge)**
  * **Where it is:** Hidden in the basement of the hotel, accessible through an unmarked door (originally an underground mailroom during Prohibition). 
  * **The Vibe:** Low lights, plush seating, exposed brick, and a quiet, intimate atmosphere. It feels like stepping straight back into 1935.
  * **The Drinks:** High-end craft cocktails with Prohibition-era roots, custom-made ice, and a deep whiskey selection.
  * *Tip:* Reservations are highly recommended for P.S., as space is very limited. 

---

### The Runner-Up: **Hotel Kansas City (In The Unbound Collection by Hyatt)**

If Hotel Phillips is fully booked, this is an incredible second option located just a few blocks away.

* **The Romantic & Historic Vibe:** Housed in the former Kansas City Club building (built in 1922), this hotel blends 1920s Gothic revival architecture with modern luxury. Think stained-glass windows, intricate woodwork, grand fireplaces, and sweeping staircases. It is wildly romantic.
* **The "Speakeasy" Bar:** **Nighthawk**
  * **Where it is:** Located in the basement of the hotel.
  * **The Vibe:** While more of a subterranean vinyl lounge than a traditional Prohibition speakeasy, it has the exact same hidden, dark, and sexy atmosphere. It features comfort food, retro cocktails, local DJs spinning vinyl, and live acoustic sets. 

---

### A Romantic Itinerary Tip for Your Stay:
Both hotels are located in the heart of Downtown KC. From either hotel, you can:
1. Walk to the **Power & Light District** or take a quick, free ride on the **KC Streetcar** down to the **Crossroads Arts District**.
2. Have a romantic dinner at **The Town Company** (inside Hotel Kansas City) or **Taillieur** (a short streetcar ride away, very romantic French bistro).
3. End your night sneaking into **P.S. Speakeasy** for a nightcap.

Kansas City has a fantastic lineup of historic, beautifully restored landmark hotels downtown, making it an ideal city for a milestone celebration. 

Here are three distinct, top-tier options for a landmark hotel stay paired with an unforgettable celebration dinner, depending on the vibe you are looking for:

---

### Option 1: The Art Deco Glamour Experience
**Hotel:** **Hotel Phillips Kansas City** *(Curio Collection by Hilton)*
* **The Landmark:** Opened in 1931, this 20-story Art Deco masterpiece was once the tallest building in Kansas City. It features gorgeous gilded details, original marble, and an iconic 11-foot bronze statue of Dawn (the goddess of morning) in the lobby.
* **The Celebration Dinner:** **Tavernonna Italian Accent** (Located inside the hotel)
  * *The Vibe:* Warm, upscale, and romantic. 
  * *The Food:* House-made pastas, wood-fired meats, and an outstanding Italian wine list.
* **Nightcap / Celebration Touch:** Head down to **P.S. Speakeasy**, a hidden cocktail bar located in the basement of the hotel (accessible through a hidden door). It feels straight out of the Prohibition era.

---

### Option 2: Historic Heritage Meets Modern Fine Dining
**Hotel:** **21c Museum Hotel Kansas City** *(The Historic Savoy Building)*
* **The Landmark:** Housed in the historic Savoy Hotel building (originally built in 1888), this property blends 19th-century architecture with a modern, boutique contemporary art museum that is open 24/7.
* **The Celebration Dinner:** **The Savoy at 21c**
  * *The Vibe:* Elegant, storied, and unique. You can ask to sit in the historic "Pendergast Booth" or Harry S. Truman’s favorite booth.
  * *The Food:* High-end, chef-driven American cuisine with an incredible seafood and steak program. 
* **Celebration Touch:** Grab a craft cocktail at the bar and stroll through the modern art galleries on the main floor with your drinks late into the evening.

---

### Option 3: Pure 1920s KC History & Jazz Age Charm
**Hotel:** **The Hilton President Kansas City**
* **The Landmark:** Opened in 1926, The President is deeply woven into KC history. It served as the headquarters for the 1928 Republican National Convention and hosted everyone from Frank Sinatra to Charles Lindbergh. 
* **The Celebration Dinner:** **The Drum Room Lounge** (Onsite) or **The Majestic Restaurant** (2-minute Uber ride)
  * *Option A (Onsite):* **The Drum Room** is a legendary KC lounge where Patsy Cline, Frank Sinatra, and Benny Goodman played. It offers classic upscale American dining.
  * *Option B (Nearby):* **The Majestic** is an authentic KC steakhouse housed in a historic former saloon/brothel, complete with live jazz playing downstairs while you eat prime steaks.

---

### Alternative: A Modern Landmark Option
If you prefer sweeping skyline views and modern luxury over 1920s history, consider **Loews Kansas City Hotel**. 
* **The Vibe:** Brand new, grand, and sleek.
* **Dinner:** Eat at **The Stillwell** inside the hotel for upscale regional cuisine with floor-to-ceiling city views, followed by drinks on their heated rooftop terrace, **Horsefeather Social**.

---

### Tips to Elevate the Night:
1. **Mention the Occasion:** When booking your room and dinner reservation, note that you are celebrating (anniversary, birthday, etc.). KC hospitality runs deep, and hotels/restaurants here frequently send up complimentary champagne or dessert.
2. **Room Choice:** At Hotel Phillips or The Savoy/21c, ask for a corner suite or a higher floor to get the best views of the downtown skyline.

Here are some solid options to consider:

- **The Loews Kansas City Hotel** - Modern, well-equipped fitness center, relatively quiet rooms

- **Hotel Phillips (Curio Collection)** - Historic boutique feel, quieter atmosphere

- **Request interior-facing rooms** if available

- Pool availability if that matters to you
- Whether the gym has the specific equipment you need

Kansas City offers a rich urban experience, especially for those interested in jazz, barbecue, and downtown exploration. Here are some recommendations for hotels that will place you in the heart of the action:

1. **The Fontaine**: Located on the Country Club Plaza, this luxurious hotel provides easy access to both downtown and the historic 18th & Vine Jazz District. The Fontaine offers stylish rooms and a rooftop pool with great city views.

For the full Kansas City experience, don't miss visiting the American Jazz Museum, indulging in some world-famous Kansas City barbecue at places like Joe's Kansas City Bar-B-Que or Arthur Bryant's, and exploring the dynamic neighborhoods downtown.

The absolute best match for your request is **Hotel Phillips Kansas City, Curio Collection by Hilton**. 

It is the premier historic Art Deco hotel in downtown Kansas City and is exceptionally well-suited for business travelers.

---

### **Top Choice: Hotel Phillips Kansas City**

* **The Art Deco Credentials:** Opened in 1931, this 20-story hotel is on the National Register of Historic Places. It is a masterpiece of Art Deco design, featuring elaborate bronze metalwork, gorgeous walnut paneling, gilded detail, and an iconic 11-foot bronze statue of "Dawn" (the goddess of morning) dominating the lobby. 
* **Business Travel Amenities:**
  * **Location:** Located at 12th & Baltimore in the heart of the Financial District. It is just two blocks from the **Kansas City Convention Center** and a short walk to the **Power & Light District**.
  * **Transit:** It is steps away from the **KC Streetcar** line (which is free to ride), giving you easy access to Union Station, Crown Center, and the River Market.
  * **Work Space:** Rooms feature well-lit dedicated work desks, fast Wi-Fi, and quiet, thick-walled construction typical of 1930s buildings.
  * **Loyalty Program:** As part of Hilton’s *Curio Collection*, you can earn or use Hilton Honors points.
* **Dining & Entertaining Clients:**
  * **Tavernonna Italian Kitchen:** Excellent upscale on-site restaurant, great for business breakfasts, lunches, or dinners.
  * **P.S. Speakeasy:** A hidden underground cocktail bar located in the hotel’s former mailroom/basement. It has a fantastic, quiet 1930s vibe—ideal for an impressive post-meeting drink with clients or colleagues.

---

### **Runner-Up / Alternative: Hilton President Kansas City**

If Hotel Phillips is booked, the **Hilton President** is your next best option.

* **The Vibe:** Opened in 1926, it is slightly earlier than the peak Art Deco era (featuring a mix of 1920s Neo-Renaissance and early Deco elements), but it carries the same historic, grand-hotel atmosphere. 
* **Business Perks:** It sits directly adjacent to the Power & Light District, making it slightly closer to the nightlife/entertainment strip, and offers full Hilton business amenities, including executive rooms, meeting spaces, and the famous **Drum Room** lounge (which hosted Frank Sinatra and Patsy Cline).

---

### **Summary Recommendation for Your Trip:**
Book **Hotel Phillips**. It nails the 1930s Art Deco aesthetic while providing all the modern digital and practical amenities required for a seamless business trip.

Staying near the Power & Light (P&L) District puts you steps away from Kansas City’s premier entertainment hub, which features over 50 bars, restaurants, live music venues (like the KC Live! Block), and the T-Mobile Center. 

Here are the best places to stay near the Power & Light District, categorized by the vibe and experience you’re looking for:

---

### 1. Directly in the Action (1–3 Minute Walk)

**Hilton President Kansas City**
* **Vibe:** Historic elegance with a lively lounge scene.
* **Why stay here:** It is literally located on the edge of the Power & Light District (14th & Baltimore). You can walk out the front door and be at the bars in seconds. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** Home to **The Drum Room**, a historic cocktail lounge that has hosted Frank Sinatra and Patsy Cline and still features live music and great drinks.

**Hotel Phillips Kansas City (Curio Collection by Hilton)**
* **Vibe:** 1920s Art Deco glam with a sultry, hidden nightlife scene.
* **Why stay here:** Located just 2 blocks from P&L, this historic hotel offers high-end accommodations with a lot of character.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** It houses **P.S. Speakeasy**, an underground, prohibition-style cocktail lounge hidden behind a fake door in the basement—perfect for a late-night nightcap.

---

### 2. High-End & Modern Luxury (3–5 Minute Walk)

**Loews Kansas City Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Modern, upscale, and buzzing with energy.
* **Why stay here:** This is one of KC’s newest and grandest hotels. It features an indoor lap pool, floor-to-ceiling skyline views, and a massive lobby bar. It’s a 5-minute walk to P&L and connected via a skybridge to the Convention Center.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** **Horsefeather Social**, the hotel's 7th-floor outdoor terrace bar, offers incredible views of downtown and the Kauffman Center, making it a top spot for pre-game or pre-concert drinks.

---

### 3. Best Value & Convenience (On the Streetcar Line)

**Courtyard & Residence Inn Kansas City Downtown/Convention Center**
* **Vibe:** Modern, reliable, and practical.
* **Why stay here:** These two Marriott properties share a single building just 2 blocks west of P&L. 
* **Nightlife Bonus:** There is a **KC Streetcar stop right outside the door**. The Streetcar is **100% free** and runs late on weekends, allowing you to easily hop between Power & Light and the trendy Crossroads Arts District just south.

---

### 4. Alternative Nightlife Scene: The Crossroads District (5 Minutes Away via Free Streetcar)

**Crossroads Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Ultra-trendy, industrial-chic, and boutique.
* **Why stay here:** Located about 6 blocks south of P&L (a 10-minute walk or a 2-minute free Streetcar ride). It is surrounded by KC’s best local breweries and cocktail bars.
* **Nightlife Bonus:** Home to **Percheron**, one of the best rooftop bars in Kansas City, offering craft beer, frozen cocktails, and panoramic views of the city.

---

### Pro-Tips for Staying Near P&L for Nightlife:

1. **Use the KC Streetcar:** It’s completely free, runs along Main Street, and operates until 1:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays. It connects P&L to Union Station, River Market, and the Crossroads.
2. **Book Ahead for Major Events:** If there is a big concert or sporting event at the **T-Mobile Center** or a Chiefs/Royals victory rally, hotels right in P&L sell out months in advance and raise rates significantly.
3. **Noise Consideration:** If you stay at the *Hilton President* or *Hotel Phillips*, request a higher floor if you are a light sleeper, as street noise and music from P&L can carry on weekend nights until 3:00 AM.

It hits every single detail you are looking for: it is deeply historic, dripping with romantic 1930s glamour, and houses one of the best hidden speakeasies in the city.

Here is the breakdown of why this is your best option, along with a top runner-up:

---

### The Top Choice: **Hotel Phillips Kansas City**

* **The Romantic & Historic Vibe:** Opened in 1931 during the height of Kansas City’s mob-ruled "Pendergast Era," Hotel Phillips is an Art Deco masterpiece listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The lobby features dark wood paneling, rich velvet, glowing vintage light fixtures, and an iconic 11-foot bronze statue of Dawn, the Goddess of a New Day. It feels moody, intimate, and sophisticated.
* **The Speakeasy:** **P.S. Speakeasy (PS Lounge)**
  * **Where it is:** Hidden in the basement of the hotel, accessible through an unmarked door (originally an underground mailroom during Prohibition). 
  * **The Vibe:** Low lights, plush seating, exposed brick, and a quiet, intimate atmosphere. It feels like stepping straight back into 1935.
  * **The Drinks:** High-end craft cocktails with Prohibition-era roots, custom-made ice, and a deep whiskey selection.
  * *Tip:* Reservations are highly recommended for P.S., as space is very limited. 

---

### The Runner-Up: **Hotel Kansas City (In The Unbound Collection by Hyatt)**

If Hotel Phillips is fully booked, this is an incredible second option located just a few blocks away.

* **The Romantic & Historic Vibe:** Housed in the former Kansas City Club building (built in 1922), this hotel blends 1920s Gothic revival architecture with modern luxury. Think stained-glass windows, intricate woodwork, grand fireplaces, and sweeping staircases. It is wildly romantic.
* **The "Speakeasy" Bar:** **Nighthawk**
  * **Where it is:** Located in the basement of the hotel.
  * **The Vibe:** While more of a subterranean vinyl lounge than a traditional Prohibition speakeasy, it has the exact same hidden, dark, and sexy atmosphere. It features comfort food, retro cocktails, local DJs spinning vinyl, and live acoustic sets. 

---

### A Romantic Itinerary Tip for Your Stay:
Both hotels are located in the heart of Downtown KC. From either hotel, you can:
1. Walk to the **Power & Light District** or take a quick, free ride on the **KC Streetcar** down to the **Crossroads Arts District**.
2. Have a romantic dinner at **The Town Company** (inside Hotel Kansas City) or **Taillieur** (a short streetcar ride away, very romantic French bistro).
3. End your night sneaking into **P.S. Speakeasy** for a nightcap.
